claims.text: In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction combined with thermogravimetric analysis can monitor high-temperature oxidation and phase stability.
The combined method reveals oxidation kinetics in real time.
The combined method reveals phase transformations in real time.
Some oxidation kinetics and phase transformations detectable in situ are not detectable by ex situ methods.
The proposed method is applicable to high-temperature alloys or ceramic coatings that are initially unoxidized or partially oxidized.
Measurements are to be performed in a controlled oxidizing atmosphere during continuous high-temperature exposure.
A temperature range of approximately 800°C to 1500°C is suitable for the proposed measurements.
Crystalline oxide phases form and evolve on the material surface during oxidation.
In situ HT-XRD tracks dynamic crystalline phase changes during oxidation.
TGA captures weight gain associated with oxide formation.
Coupling HT-XRD phase measurements with TGA mass measurements provides information about phase stability and oxidation kinetics.
The integrated measurement will produce time-resolved crystalline-phase transitions correlated with weight changes.
Correlated phase and mass changes can reveal oxide-scale formation and phase-transformation mechanisms as they occur.
Ex situ oxidation testing relies on heat treatment followed by weight-gain measurement and post-mortem microstructural analysis.
Measurement results may depend on material composition and oxidation temperature.
Limited measurement time resolution may prevent detection of fast phase transitions.
